The crowd chanted France's national anthem and waved flags, and some people played trumpets and violins.
In Lyon, France's third-largest city where about 20,000 protesters joined the march, a fire broke out inside a tourist office.
In the southern port city of Marseille, some shops and a municipal police station were damaged, while protesters briefly forced their way into the lobby of City Hall.
City of Bend Police Chief Mike Krantz called the teacher's actions "heroic" during a news conference and said she was not injured.
He identified the attacker as 16-year-old Griffin J.
John II and said all of the victims were shot in the same classroom.
John was once a special needs student at Silver Rail Elementary, authorities said, and he attacked a classroom with special needs students.
He fired as many as 15 shots from a 12-gauge shotgun and had about 44 rounds remaining when he was killed, Krantz said.
"Everyone wants to know why, including us," he said. "We may never get that full answer, but we want it."
She declined to say how the 16-year-old obtained the pump-action shotgun and didn’t comment further when The Associated Press and other outlets knocked on her apartment door later.
In a 2020 interview with the local news station KTVZ, Nickerson identified the boy, then 10, as a participant in a special needs program run by the school district.
It was called NEST, for Nurturing Empathy, Safety and Trust, and aimed at helping students experiencing intensive behavioral and social skill challenges.
Nickerson said he struggled trying to learn from home during the pandemic.
The first 911 call came from the driver of a red pickup truck early Thursday afternoon who saw the boy throw his gun over a fence outside the school and then climb over it, Krantz said.
The driver yelled at the boy, who fired at him, striking the truck three times.
The driver was not injured.
A second driver, Kaylub Giamanco, a 36-year-old man whose children attend Silver Rail, saw John shooting at the truck and heading toward the school, where he shot through locked doors to get inside. Giamanco pulled into the parking lot, grabbed his .40-caliber pistol and followed the attacker inside.
He saw John wrestling with the teacher and shot him several times.
Three children — ages 5, 8 and 11 — and teacher Megan Lambert, 25, were killed, police said.
A 7-year-old child who was injured received lifesaving care at the scene and is now hospitalized, as is 54-year-old teacher Becky Drury, who her family said was shot in the arm and hand and was recovering from surgery.
